title: Testimony by Vice Chair for Supervision Quarles on supervision and regulation - Federal Reserve Board
主要内容: On May 19, 2021, Federal Reserve Vice Chair Quarles testified about the U.S. banking sector's recovery post-COVID-19. The banking system, strengthened by over 10 years of reforms, absorbed unprecedented shocks while supporting public aid and borrowers. The recovery was aided by coordinated efforts from Congress and the Federal Reserve. Post-2008 reforms ensured a different outcome compared to the 2008 crisis. The Federal Reserve Board emphasized that the banking system is more liquid and better capitalized than a year ago, with over $100 billion in additional loan loss reserves. The system is well-positioned to weather future shocks. While a strong recovery is underway, it is not yet complete. Policymakers aim to support the financial system and economy through the transition back to normal operations. The Fed has aligned emergency actions with other relief efforts, maintained or extended some measures to preserve household assistance and promote credit access, and begun transitioning back to normal supervisory activities. These steps are part of a responsible transition out of the emergency posture.
